verdict: No material correctness or scope issue found in the frozen two-file implementation and its bound local regression evidence. This is source review, not deployment or user acceptance.

sourceAssessment.finding: reload captures active context/request epoch plus generation and original broker. Both HTTP/package digest completion boundaries recheck this owner before global package, delivery, hidden-state or publish work. The publish call uses the captured broker.

An operation that itself increments generation and disposes/chooses a view refreshes only its own ownership snapshot immediately after the synchronous transition. Post-disposal current checks prevent a later view/scope from receiving stale empty-package side effects. choose internally owns the full package/context/token lifetime.

Old broker close can reject pending publish, but the stale catch cannot latch failedPackageIdentity, dispose a successor or change its status. A current error retains failure latch, owned disposal and retry UI; after awaited disposal it checks ownership again.

choose preserves the existing original-local start/close lifecycle. Its catch now rechecks its token/context/package after asynchronous disposal before setting current failure UI, so a late old error cannot repaint a newer choice.

Polling remains owned by active context/request epoch, independently of view generation. A view switch therefore retains one continuation; a newer reload, setActive(false), leave or pagehide invalidates the old epoch and prevents late timer rearming. Existing request clearTimeout and epoch guards avoid parallel continuations.

Broker authorization, before/after delivery checks, cancellation, request budgets, port ownership and fail-closed callbacks are unchanged. Current-owner 403 and actual stalled HTTP remain latch/close cases; an automatic package200 cannot reexecute the failed package until explicit Retry.

regressionAssessment: The new fixture uses the actual opaque native frame and product broker. Only the 60s panel poll timer and a marked API delivery are controlled; it does not replace authorization/deadline behavior.

The initial real subscribed Dashboard is confirmed before one old package/publish result is deferred. Host Report is selected once; both resolve and reject paths wait for an explicit Report-ready or final error marker, not an arbitrary sleep or iframe attachment alone.

Four deferred cases assert Report selection/readiness, original port closed, one continuation and successful subsequent real read-only poll. A second deferred package result followed by leave verifies no frame resurrection, timer continuation or old message handler.

403 and a genuinely stalled HTTP response retain current-owner fail-closed behavior and same-package latch; explicit Retry restores the frame. The stall is aborted on the unchanged10s inner HTTP deadline.

The first insufficiently-awaited red-v1 and the initial missing-default-WebKit-runtime invocation remain separate failed history; neither is counted as a product red proof or a successful regression. Corrected red-v2 uses the exact final test body and old production bytes.
scopeAndLimits: Production changes are limited to project-views.js ownership and asynchronous side-effect checks. No backend, Gateway route, SDK API, frame protocol, deadline, provider, scope, authorization, fallback or capacity change.
Chromium29 includes the six new cases; focused Chromium6 repeats that subset, and WebKit6 is another browser execution of the same new cases. These are not41 unique new tests.
The evidence reproduces one deterministic stale-owner race and its local fix; it does not establish the original online Report failure as uniquely caused by that race.

Existing browser tests retain synthetic model/artifact fixtures and loopback HTTP only. No Safari, real project, provider, paid Turn, Cloudflare, Registry or AMD execution is performed by this review.
This review creates no merge, deployment, gate, retry, new user execution authorization or Done/Issue closure claim. Original fb07 history and time bounds remain intact.

Receipt source hashes are recorded by the author runner after command completion; independent current/base/patch/snapshot equality and exact raw output hashes were checked here. This is not a new test execution or independent runtime instrumentation.
